commits.title: Workflow runs are claimed and run by one engine, with a scope for the stores and one for the platform

changes.how: A new server-only module (`import "server-only"`). It holds the part of runWorkflows() (src/server/workflows.ts, from `const claimed = await typedRows(` to the final `return`) and of runPlatformWorkflows() (src/server/platform-workflows.ts, the same span) that is the same in both. Export a type `WorkflowScope<Run>` with these members, and nothing read from a string: `runs: SQL` and `flows: SQL` (the two table names as drizzle sql fragments written in code, for example sql`commerce.workflow_runs` and sql`commerce.workflows`; never sql.raw), `returning: SQL` (the columns the claim's update returns, each prefixed `r.`), `select: SQL` (everything after `select c.*, w.name, w.conditions, w.actions` up to the end of the statement: the extra columns and the joins), `row: z.ZodType<Run>` (the zod object for one claimed row; it must include id, workflow_id, event, subject_id, name, conditions, actions), `payloadOf: (run: Run) => Promise<Record<string, unknown> | null>` (the event's facts for every event, 'schedule' included: {} for a schedule, null when the subject is gone or the owner is not open; the engine never decides this itself), `allowedActions: (event: string) => readonly string[]`, `act: (run: Run, action: WorkflowAction, index: number, data: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<ActionOutcome>`, `logPrefix: string` ('workflows' or 'platform_workflows') and `logFields: (run: Run) => Record<string, unknown>`. Export `async function runQueued<Run>(scope: WorkflowScope<Run>, limit: number): Promise<{ runs: number; matched: number }>`. Its body, in this order, is the stores' code with the scope's parts put in: (1) the claim statement exactly as today: `with due as (select r.id from ${scope.runs} r where r.status = 'pending' and (r.claimed_until is null or r.claimed_until < now()) order by r.created_at limit ${limit} for update skip locked), claimed as (update ${scope.runs} r set claimed_until = now() + interval '5 minutes' from due where r.id = due.id returning ${scope.returning}) select c.*, w.name, w.conditions, w.actions ${scope.select}` read through typedRows(scope.row, ...); (2) the loop: for each run, data = await scope.payloadOf(run); matched = data !== null && workflowMatches(conditions, data); for each action, 'invalid' when not in scope.allowedActions(run.event), else scope.act(...) with the catch that logs `${scope.logPrefix}.action_failed` and returns { kind, ok: false, problem: 'failed' }; (3) the outcome update on ${scope.runs} with the same status, matched, outcome JSON, finished_at and claimed_until = null, `where id = ${run.id}::uuid`; the per-run catch logs `${scope.logPrefix}.run_failed`; (4) `delete from ${scope.runs} where created_at < now() - interval '90 days'`; (5) the return. Import workflowMatches, WorkflowAction, WorkflowCondition and ActionOutcome from where workflows.ts imports them.

runWorkflows(limit = 50, now = new Date()) keeps its name, arguments and result. Its body becomes: `await queueScheduledRuns(now); return runQueued(STORE_SCOPE, limit);`. Define STORE_SCOPE in this file: runs sql`commerce.workflow_runs`, flows sql`commerce.workflows`, returning `r.id, r.store_id, r.workflow_id, r.event, r.subject_id`, select `, coalesce(w.updated_by, w.created_by) as account, s.slug, s.name as store_name, commerce.store_is_active(s.id) as open from claimed c join commerce.workflows w on w.id = c.workflow_id join commerce.stores s on s.id = c.store_id`, row = the zod object the function has today, payloadOf = (run) => !run.open ? null : run.event === 'schedule' ? {} : subjectData({ id: run.store_id, slug: run.slug, name: run.store_name }, run.event, run.subject_id) (a store that is not open runs nothing, a scheduled run included: today's code sets data to null after reading it when the store is not open; keep that result), allowedActions = (event) => actionsFor(event === 'schedule' ? 'schedule' : (event as WorkflowTrigger)), act = the file's own act() called with the same object as today, logPrefix 'workflows', logFields = { storeId, workflowId }. Note one order difference to keep identical: today subjectData() is called even for a closed store and then discarded; calling it only when open changes no result. Leave queueScheduledRuns(), workflowRuns(), the editor functions and every export as they are.

runPlatformWorkflows(limit = 25, now = new Date()) becomes `await queuePlatformScheduledRuns(now); return runQueued(PLATFORM_SCOPE, limit);`. PLATFORM_SCOPE: runs sql`commerce.platform_workflow_runs`, flows sql`commerce.platform_workflows`, returning `r.id, r.workflow_id, r.event, r.subject_id, r.created_at`, select ` from claimed c join commerce.platform_workflows w on w.id = c.workflow_id`, row = today's zod object, payloadOf = (run) => run.event === 'schedule' ? {} : platformPayload({ id: run.id, event: run.event, subjectId: run.subject_id, createdAt: run.created_at }), allowedActions = (event) => PLATFORM_WORKFLOWS.actionsFor(event), act = the file's own act({ id, event, subjectId, name }, action, index), logPrefix 'platform_workflows', logFields = { workflowId }. Everything else in the file stays, including the strict tested-version check of D516 in switchPlatformWorkflow().

commits.title: Own endpoints are kept by one store of endpoints, with a scope

changes.how: Server-only. Holds once what src/server/webhook-endpoints.ts and src/server/platform-endpoints.ts both write: check() (name, topics, address), newSecret(), topicArray(), and the bodies of add, update, switch, renew secret, remove, resend delivery and list deliveries. Export `type EndpointScope = { table: SQL; deliveries: SQL; owned: SQL; lock: SQL; insertColumns: SQL; insertValues: SQL; topicsAllowed: (topic: string) => boolean; audit: (action: 'added' | 'changed' | 'switched' | 'secret_renewed' | 'removed' | 'resent', meta: Record<string, unknown>, id: string) => Promise<void> }`. `owned` is the owner clause: for a store sql`store_id = ${storeId}::uuid and app_grant_id is null`, for the platform sql`true`. `lock` is the advisory lock's key expression as each file writes it today. Every statement that picks a row by id is written `where ${scope.owned} and id = ${id}::uuid` in that order (the form src/server/ratchet.scan.test.ts accepts as naming the store). The limit ENDPOINTS_MAX, FAILING_DAYS and the exported types stay in webhook-endpoints.ts and are imported here as types or constants.

addEndpoint, updateEndpoint, switchEndpoint, renewSecret, removeEndpoint, resendDelivery and listEndpointDeliveries keep their exported names, arguments and results and become short calls of the store's functions with a scope built from the membership: table sql`commerce.webhook_endpoints`, deliveries sql`commerce.integration_deliveries`, the owned clause above, audit names exactly as today (read them off the file: each audit() call's action string and target type 'webhook_endpoint'). listEndpoints() and openEndpoint() stay as they are.

The same seven functions (addPlatformEndpoint ... listPlatformEndpointDeliveries) become calls with the platform's scope: table sql`commerce.platform_webhook_endpoints`, deliveries sql`commerce.platform_integration_deliveries`, owned sql`true`, lock `hashtext('platform_webhook_endpoints')`, audit names 'platform.endpoint_added', 'platform.endpoint_changed' and the others as the file has them, target type 'platform_webhook_endpoint', store null. listPlatformEndpoints() and keepPlatformEndpointHealth() stay.

commits.title: Integration deliveries are claimed, sent and retried by one loop, with a scope

changes.how: Server-only. Holds once the body shared by deliverDue() (src/server/integrations.ts) and deliverPlatformDue() (src/server/platform-integrations.ts): `export async function deliverQueued<D>(scope: { table: SQL; read: (ids: string[]) => Promise<D[]>; attempt: (delivery: D) => Promise<Outcome>; retryable: (delivery: D) => boolean; keepDays: number }, limit: number)`. Body: the claim `update ${scope.table} set next_attempt_at = now() + interval '5 minutes' where id in (select id from ${scope.table} where status = 'pending' and next_attempt_at <= now() order by next_attempt_at limit ${limit} for update skip locked) returning id`; then scope.read(ids) (empty list: no query); the counting loop (delivered when outcome.ok; retrying when !outcome.final and scope.retryable(delivery); else failed); the delete of rows older than scope.keepDays; return counts. Each side keeps its own attempt(), its payload builder, its signing call and its claimed-row reader; the shared signer and sender they both already import stay where they are.

deliverDue(limit = 50) becomes a call of deliverQueued() with table sql`commerce.integration_deliveries`, read = the existing select with claimedColumns and its three joins mapped through toClaimed(), attempt, retryable = (d) => RETRY_SECONDS[d.attempts] !== undefined && Boolean(d.encryptedUrl) && d.enabled, keepDays KEEP_DAYS. Nothing else in the file changes.

deliverPlatformDue(limit = 25) becomes a call with table sql`commerce.platform_integration_deliveries`, read = the existing typedRows(claimedRow, ...) select, attempt, retryable = (d) => RETRY_SECONDS[d.attempts] !== undefined && Boolean(d.webhook_url_encrypted) && d.enabled, keepDays PLATFORM_DELIVERY_KEEP_DAYS.
